pairs.description: Pairs of doodle cards in the heap. Setting it replaces the built-in progression (5, 10, 15 ... 40 pairs over 8 levels) for the level in play and every later level: pairs are dealt into the heap or taken out of it immediately. More pairs mean a bigger heap to search.
pairs.adjustment_guide: The main load lever. Raise in steps of 2-5 while the player matches quickly with few UNMATCH events (short gaps between MATCH events). Lower when UNMATCH events pile up or the gaps between MATCH events grow long. LEVEL_START and OBJECTIVES_CHANGED report the pairs in play as objectives.

clusterSpread.description: Size of the heap the cards are scattered in, as a multiple of the game's own (which grows with the number of cards). Lower values pack the cards tighter so more of them overlap and hide each other; higher values spread them out. Applies to the heap in play immediately.
clusterSpread.adjustment_guide: Lower (0.5-0.8) for focus and attention training, since overlapping cards must be uncovered or dragged apart. Raise (1.3-2.0) for relax or a struggling player so every doodle is visible at a glance.

cardRotation.description: Largest tilt of a card in the heap, in degrees. 0 = every card upright, 180 = any orientation (the game's default). Applies to the heap in play immediately; cards the player drags still spin a little.
cardRotation.adjustment_guide: Lower (0-45) for relax, joy or a struggling player so doodles are easy to recognise. Keep 120-180 for spatial and pattern-matching training, where the player has to recognise a rotated doodle.

adjustment_instructions:
Match Doodle: a heap of doodle cards sits on the table; one card is dealt onto the drop pad and the player finds its twin in the heap and drags it onto the pad. A wrong card bounces back. A level ends when every pair is matched; there is no time limit (the clock counts up).
Levers: pairs is the main load lever (more cards to search); clusterSpread sets how tightly the heap is packed (lower = more overlap); cardRotation sets how tilted the cards are (higher = harder to recognise).
- relax: pairs 4-8, clusterSpread 1.3-2.0, cardRotation 0-45.
- focus: pairs 10-20, clusterSpread 0.6-0.9, cardRotation 90-180.
- grit: pairs 20-40, clusterSpread 0.5-0.7, cardRotation 180; ease pairs down when UNMATCH events pile up.
- joy: pairs 5-12, clusterSpread 1.0-1.5, cardRotation 0-90 (quick, satisfying matches).
Change pairs in steps of 2-5. Ease clusterSpread up before cutting pairs when a player is stuck.
skill_adjustment_instructions:
Match Doodle trains Pattern Matching and Perceptual Speed (visual search for a doodle's twin), with Attention (ignoring look-alike distractors) and Spatial (recognising rotated doodles).
- pattern matching, perceptual speed: raise pairs (15-40) so the search set is large; clusterSpread 0.8-1.2 so cards stay visible.
- attention: clusterSpread 0.5-0.8 so cards overlap and must be uncovered; pairs 10-25.
- spatial: cardRotation 120-180 with moderate pairs (8-15), so recognising rotated doodles is the challenge.
- action: moderate pairs (8-15) and clusterSpread 0.6-0.9, so dragging cards apart and onto the pad is part of the challenge.
notes: Match Doodle's difficulty knobs, matching static/skillprintShim.js, ../parameters.json and GameAdjustmentTester's 'match-doodle' keys. `pairs` keeps its old name; it used to take effect only at the next level and now applies to the level in play.
